security_audit.summary: The skill contains no prompt injection or evidence of malicious exfiltration. Several static findings are markdown false positives, but real package manager and script commands remain. Those commands can execute project or downloaded package code; the URLs point to official Next.js documentation.

remediation.issue: Package manager and codemod commands may execute downloaded or project code.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running npx, npm install, npm run build, or npm run dev, and show the exact command first.

remediation.issue: Commands use @latest, which can change behavior over time.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a user-approved target version or record the resolved package versions before applying changes.

remediation.issue: Codemods and installs can make broad file changes.
remediation.suggestion: Instruct agents to confirm a clean git branch and summarize diffs after each step.

content.value_statement: Next.js upgrades can break routing, types, dependencies, and build behavior. This skill guides agents through official docs, codemods, dependency updates, and validation steps.
actual_capabilities: Reads package metadata to identify current Next.js, React, and React DOM versions.
Directs the agent to official Next.js upgrade and codemod documentation.
Maps major version jumps into incremental migration steps.
Recommends official Next.js codemods for common breaking changes.
Guides dependency, type package, build, and development server validation commands.
limitations: It does not guarantee that every custom application behavior is migrated automatically.
It requires review of official docs because Next.js guidance changes over time.
It may run package manager commands that modify dependencies and project files.
It does not replace application-specific testing or production rollout checks.

use_cases.title: Upgrade an application
use_cases.description: Move an existing Next.js project to a newer version with guided dependency updates and codemod steps.

use_cases.title: Plan a major migration
use_cases.description: Break a large version jump into ordered tasks that follow official migration guidance.

use_cases.title: Review upgrade readiness
use_cases.description: Identify required codemods, manual breaking changes, and validation commands before changing production code.

prompt_templates.title: Start an upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Upgrade this project to the latest stable Next.js version. Start by reading package.json, explain the current version, then propose the migration steps before changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a guided upgrade

prompt_templates.title: Target a version
prompt_templates.prompt: Upgrade this project from Next.js [current] to [target]. Use official upgrade docs, run applicable codemods, update dependencies, and summarize each changed area.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with a known target version

prompt_templates.title: Plan a staged migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an incremental Next.js major-version migration for this repository. Identify risk areas, codemods, manual edits, validation commands, and rollback checkpoints before implementation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a larger repository

prompt_templates.title: Audit an upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit a completed Next.js upgrade. Compare changes against official migration guidance, inspect build and type errors, and produce a remediation checklist.

output_examples.input: Upgrade a Next.js 14 app to the latest stable release.
output_examples.output: A migration plan covering official docs checked, codemods to run, dependency updates, manual breaking changes, and validation results.

output_examples.input: Review this repository after running Next.js codemods.
output_examples.output: A concise audit of remaining async request API changes, config updates, dependency issues, and tests still needed.

best_practices: Review the migration plan and approve package manager commands before they run.
Work from a clean branch so codemod and dependency changes are easy to inspect.
Run build, type checks, tests, and manual routes after each major version step.
anti_patterns: Do not jump multiple major versions without checking each official guide.
Do not accept codemod changes without reviewing the diff.
Do not rely on install success as proof that the application still works.

faq.question: Does this skill use official Next.js documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs the agent to fetch official Next.js upgrade and codemod guides.

faq.question: Can it upgrade across multiple major versions?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs incremental upgrades when major versions are skipped.

faq.question: Will it edit project files?
faq.answer: It can guide codemods and dependency updates, so project files may change.

faq.question: Does it support TypeScript projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for React type package updates when TypeScript is used.

faq.question: Is it safe to run on any repository?
faq.answer: Use a clean branch and review commands first because package tools can execute project scripts.

faq.question: Does it replace testing?
faq.answer: No. It requires build checks and manual testing of key application behavior.
